entries.description: Outperformed LLaMA 2 13B at 7B parameters. Sliding window attention + grouped query attention as architecture innovations. Showed aggressive data quality scaling matters more than parameter count.

entries.title: Mixtral of Experts
entries.description: Sparse Mixture of Experts with 8 experts, 2 active per token. 46.7B parameters, 12.9B active. GPT-3.5 quality at 6× lower inference cost. Validated MoE as practical architecture.

entries.title: MobileNets: Efficient CNNs for Mobile Vision
entries.description: Depthwise separable convolutions reduce compute 8–9× vs. standard convolutions with minimal accuracy loss. Defined the mobile inference paradigm.

entries.title: MuZero: Mastering Atari, Go, Chess and Shogi by Planning with a Learned Model
entries.description: AlphaZero required knowledge of the game rules to plan with MCTS. MuZero learns a model of the environment purely from experience — without any simulator — and uses that learned model for planning. Achieves superhuman performance in Atari, Go, Chess, and Shogi without being given the rules.

entries.title: Neural Architecture Search with Reinforcement Learning (NASNet)
entries.description: Showed architectures could be designed by algorithms, not just humans. Started the AutoML field. Led to EfficientNet which dominated image classification benchmarks for years.

entries.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
entries.description: Invented attention for NLP. Solved the bottleneck problem of compressing long sequences into one vector. Direct predecessor to self-attention and the Transformer.

entries.title: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)
entries.description: Implicit neural representation of 3D scenes. Generate photorealistic novel views from sparse 2D images. Revolutionized 3D reconstruction and spawned 3D Gaussian Splatting.

entries.title: ONNX: Open Neural Network Exchange
entries.description: ONNX defines a common intermediate representation for neural network models, enabling models trained in one framework (PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn) to be deployed in any other runtime (TensorRT, OpenVINO, CoreML, ONNX Runtime). Solves the train-in-one-place, deploy-everywhere problem.

entries.title: OpenAI o1 Technical Report: Learning to Reason with LLMs
entries.description: Demonstrates that training LLMs to use extended internal reasoning chains ("thinking") before answering dramatically improves performance on competition math, coding, and scientific reasoning. o1 uses reinforcement learning over a reasoning process rather than just the final answer. Establishes the "inference-time compute" scaling paradigm: more compute at test time → better answers.

entries.title: Orca: A Distributed Serving System for Transformer-Based Generative Models
entries.description: Prior LLM serving batched requests together and padded all sequences to the maximum length in the batch — wasting GPU time on padding tokens. Orca introduced **continuous batching** (iteration-level scheduling): each forward pass step processes a dynamic set of tokens from different requests, and new requests join mid-batch as old ones finish. This yielded up to 36.9× throughput improvement over static batching.

entries.title: PaLI: A Jointly-Scaled Multilingual Language-Image Model
entries.description: Jointly scale vision encoder and language model. 17B parameters across 100+ languages. Best multimodal accuracy of its time. Showed multilingual multimodal is achievable.

entries.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
entries.description: PaLM â€” Google's 540B parameter model trained on Pathways; demonstrated breakthrough reasoning capabilities and discontinuous capability jumps.

entries.title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways
entries.description: Showed how a 540-billion-parameter dense Transformer could be trained efficiently across 6,144 TPU v4 chips while gaining strong few-shot reasoning and multilingual capabilities.

entries.title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding (Imagen)
entries.description: Large frozen language model (T5-XXL) as text encoder beats CLIP for text fidelity. Demonstrated that language understanding > image-text alignment for high-fidelity generation.

entries.title: PipeDream: Generalized Pipeline Parallelism for DNN Training
entries.description: Identified that GPipe's synchronous pipeline creates a bubble — all workers stall between forward and backward passes. PipeDream introduced 1F1B (one-forward-one-backward) scheduling to eliminate the bubble, interleaving forward and backward passes to keep all stages active. Introduced weight stashing to maintain consistent gradient computation.

entries.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning (DQN)
entries.description: First demonstration that deep neural networks could learn to play games directly from raw pixels better than humans. Experience replay + target network = stable deep Q-learning. Started deep RL.

entries.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels (HyDE)
entries.description: Generate a hypothetical document from the query, embed it, retrieve real documents similar to the hypothetical. Dramatically improves zero-shot retrieval by bridging query-document distribution gap.

entries.title: Proximal Policy Optimization Algorithms (PPO)
entries.description: Simple, robust on-policy RL. Clipped surrogate objective prevents too-large policy updates without second-order optimization. Default RL algorithm for 5+ years; used in InstructGPT/RLHF.

entries.title: PyTorch: An Imperative Style, High-Performance Deep Learning Library
entries.description: Define-by-run (eager execution) made debugging natural. Python-first API. Became the dominant research framework by 2019, production framework by 2022.

entries.title: PyTorch FSDP: Fully Sharded Data Parallel
entries.description: FSDP is PyTorch-native ZeRO-3: it shards model parameters, gradients, and optimizer states across data-parallel workers, and all-gathers them just-in-time during forward/backward passes. Unlike DeepSpeed ZeRO, it is fully integrated into PyTorch's autograd and module system. Used to train LLaMA 1/2/3, OPT, and other Meta models.

entries.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
entries.description: Fine-tune 65B LLaMA on a single 48GB GPU via 4-bit quantization + LoRA + paged attention. Democratized LLM fine-tuning. Guanaco-65B competitive with ChatGPT.

entries.title: RAG-Fusion: Reciprocal Rank Fusion for Better Retrieval
entries.description: A single query to a retriever captures one perspective of information need. RAG-Fusion generates multiple query variations using the LLM, retrieves documents for each, and uses Reciprocal Rank Fusion to merge the result sets into a single ranked list. Captures more facets of information need without changing the retriever.

entries.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
entries.description: Interleaved reasoning traces and actions — "Thought, Action, Observation" loop. Dramatically improved performance on QA, fact verification, decision-making benchmarks. Defined the LLM agent paradigm.

entries.title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
entries.description: REALM integrates retrieval into pretraining itself — for each masked token prediction, the model retrieves relevant documents from a knowledge corpus before predicting. The retriever and language model are trained jointly end-to-end. Knowledge is stored in an external index, not in model parameters.

entries.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
entries.description: Agents that learn from failure via verbal reflection — no gradient updates. Store failures in episodic memory, use them to improve on next trial. Self-improving agents without fine-tuning.

entries.title: Rethinking Atrous Convolution for Semantic Segmentation (DeepLab v3)
entries.description: ASPP (Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling) captures multi-scale context without reducing resolution. Encoder-decoder variant (v3+) set segmentation SOTA on multiple benchmarks.

entries.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
entries.description: Named and defined the RAG paradigm. Retriever + generator end-to-end. Open-domain QA with parametric + non-parametric memory. Every enterprise RAG system traces to this paper.

entries.title: Retrieval-Enhanced Machine Learning (REALM)
entries.description: First paper to pre-train the retriever jointly with the language model end-to-end. Retriever learns what to retrieve for language modeling. Conceptual predecessor to all RAG systems.

entries.title: Ring Attention with Blockwise Transformers
entries.description: Enables training transformers with sequences of millions of tokens by distributing the attention computation across devices in a ring topology. Each device holds a slice of the sequence and computes local attention while simultaneously sending its KV blocks around the ring. Memory per device scales as O(N/k) where k is number of devices.

entries.title: RLHF: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback
entries.description: InstructGPT paper. Demonstrates that a 1.3B RLHF-finetuned model is preferred over a 175B base model by human raters. Three-stage pipeline: supervised fine-tuning on demonstrations, reward model training from human comparisons, PPO optimization against the reward model. This is the recipe for ChatGPT and every instruction-following LLM.

entries.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
entries.description: Showed BERT was significantly undertrained. Removing NSP, training longer, using dynamic masking, and larger batches improved performance substantially. Best practices for BERT-style training.

entries.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper)
entries.description: 680,000 hours of web audio for weakly supervised ASR. Multitask (transcription, translation, language ID, timestamps). Robust zero-shot generalization — doesn't need fine-tuning for most languages.

entries.title: RoFormer: Enhanced Transformer with Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE)
entries.description: Rotary positional embeddings encode absolute position via rotation while enabling relative position computation in attention. Naturally extends to longer contexts. Now standard in LLaMA, PaLM, GPT-Neo.

entries.title: Scalable Diffusion Models with Transformers (DiT)
entries.description: Replaced U-Net backbone in diffusion with Vision Transformer. Scales better — larger DiT = better FID. Sora uses DiT-based architecture for video generation. Defined the next generation of diffusion models.

entries.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
entries.description: Discovered that LLM performance follows predictable power laws with compute, data, and parameters. Changed how AI labs plan training runs. Directly motivated GPT-3, Chinchilla, and all frontier model training.

entries.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
entries.description: Empirically establishes that language model loss follows a power law with respect to model parameters, dataset size, and compute — each independently. Shows that for a fixed compute budget, the optimal strategy is to scale parameters and data proportionally. This paper justified the investment in GPT-3 and every large model since.

entries.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations
entries.description: Unified diffusion models and score matching as continuous-time SDEs. Theoretical foundation that enables new samplers, conditioned generation, and the connections to flow matching.

entries.title: Segment Anything
entries.description: Segment Anything Model (SAM) â€” a foundational vision model capable of zero-shot segmentation from points, boxes, or text prompts.

entries.title: Segment Anything (SAM)
entries.description: Foundation model for image segmentation. Promptable (point, box, text) → mask. Trained on 1B masks. Defined the "foundation model for vision" paradigm.

entries.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
entries.description: Sample diverse reasoning paths, take majority vote answer. +17.9% on GSM8K over greedy decoding. Simple ensemble technique that dramatically improves reasoning reliability.

entries.title: Self-Instruct: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
entries.description: Bootstrap instruction data from 175 human-written seed examples using the LLM itself. Alpaca was built on this — 52K instructions generated at $500 using GPT-3.5. Democratized alignment.

entries.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
entries.description: LLM learns when to retrieve (not always) and critiques its own outputs. Reflection tokens for retrieve/relevant/supported/useful decisions. Better accuracy and factuality than standard RAG.

entries.title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
entries.description: Standard RAG always retrieves, even when not needed. Self-RAG trains a model to decide when to retrieve (or not), generate responses with or without retrieval, and critique its own outputs using special reflection tokens (ISREL, ISSUP, ISUSE). A single model handles retrieval decisions and generation quality assessment.

entries.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
entries.description: BERT is too slow for semantic similarity (O(n²) pairs). SBERT generates fixed-size sentence embeddings in a single forward pass enabling 50 million pairs per day vs. 65 hours with BERT.

entries.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings Using Siamese BERT-Networks
entries.description: BERT's cross-encoder setup requires running inference for every pair of sentences — O(N²) cost for semantic search over a corpus. SBERT uses a Siamese network to produce fixed-size sentence embeddings that can be compared with cosine similarity, enabling O(N) search. Still the most used framework for dense retrieval embeddings.

entries.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
entries.description: First demonstration that LSTMs in an encoder-decoder configuration could do machine translation competitively. Defined the sequence-to-sequence paradigm that T5 and modern generative models inherit.

entries.title: SimCSE: Simple Contrastive Learning of Sentence Embeddings
entries.description: SimCSE achieves state-of-the-art sentence embeddings using the simplest possible contrastive approach: pass the same sentence through a dropout-based encoder twice to get two views, treat them as positives, treat other sentences in the batch as negatives. Unsupervised SimCSE beats many supervised methods. Supervised SimCSE (with NLI pairs) sets the SOTA.

entries.title: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep RL
entries.description: Maximum entropy RL adds entropy bonus for exploration. SAC is sample-efficient, stable, and competitive with model-based methods. Most capable continuous control algorithm.

entries.title: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC): Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning with a Stochastic Actor
entries.description: Adds an entropy regularization term to the RL objective, encouraging policies that are both high-reward and high-entropy (exploratory). The temperature parameter α is automatically tuned. SAC is significantly more sample-efficient than TD3, more stable than DDPG, and generalizes better to new tasks. Dominant off-policy algorithm for continuous control.

entries.title: Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks (SENet)
entries.description: Channel attention via global average pooling → FC → scale. Won ILSVRC 2017. SE blocks add minimal parameters but consistent accuracy gains across architectures.

entries.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
entries.description: Stable Diffusion — the open-source release of the Latent Diffusion Model trained on LAION-5B, which democratized AI image generation.

entries.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
entries.description: Benchmark of 2,294 real GitHub issues across 12 Python repos. Tests actual software engineering — understand codebase, write patch, pass tests. Defines the AI software engineer challenge.

entries.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
entries.description: SWE-bench collects 2,294 real GitHub issues from 12 popular Python repos and requires models to generate patches that pass the associated test suite. Early models (including GPT-4 at release) solved <2% of tasks. SWE-bench-Verified (with human filtering) became the standard benchmark for coding agents. Devin's 13.86% resolved rate was a major milestone.

entries.title: Swin Transformer: Hierarchical Vision Transformer using Shifted Windows
entries.description: Made ViT practical for dense prediction tasks. Shifted window attention achieves O(n) complexity vs O(n²) for full attention. Hierarchical features enable FPN integration.

entries.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
entries.description: Switch Transformers — simplified Mixture of Experts with Top-1 routing, enabling trillion-parameter sparse models with constant per-token FLOPs.

entries.title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models with Simple and Efficient Sparsity
entries.description: Simplified mixture-of-experts routing to one expert per token, making trillion-parameter sparse language models trainable with stable and efficient infrastructure.

entries.title: T5: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
entries.description: T5 reframes every NLP task — classification, translation, summarization, QA — as text-to-text: input and output are always strings. This single formulation enabled training one model on many tasks simultaneously. T5 introduced the C4 dataset, explored scaling laws for encoders, and showed that a unified objective outperforms task-specific pretraining.

entries.title: TD3: Addressing Function Approximation Error in Actor-Critic Methods
entries.description: DDPG suffers from overestimation of Q-values due to function approximation error, causing the policy to exploit incorrect high-value actions. TD3 adds three fixes: clipped double Q-learning (take min of two Q-networks), delayed policy updates (update actor less frequently than critic), and target policy smoothing (add noise to target actions). Standard baseline for continuous control.

entries.title: TensorFlow: A System for Large-Scale Machine Learning
entries.description: First scalable, production-ready deep learning framework. Computation graph abstraction. TPU support. Deployed deep learning at Google's scale.

entries.title: TensorRT: Scalable, Efficient Deep Learning Inference
entries.description: TensorRT is NVIDIA's inference optimizer: it takes a trained model, performs layer fusion, precision calibration (INT8/FP16 quantization), kernel auto-selection, and generates a highly optimized runtime engine. Inference engines generated by TensorRT run 3–10× faster than the native framework on GPU. It is the production deployment target for most NVIDIA-GPU-based inference systems.

entries.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
entries.description: Showed that large networks contain small sparse subnetworks ("winning tickets") that can train to full accuracy. Foundational for network pruning, efficient neural networks, and mechanistic interpretability.

entries.title: ToolBench: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-World APIs
entries.description: Constructs a benchmark of 16,000+ real REST APIs from RapidAPI, generates instruction-following data for tool use, and trains ToolLLaMA via supervised fine-tuning on GPT-4-generated solutions. Introduces DFSDT (depth-first search decision tree) for solving multi-step tool use problems.

entries.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
entries.description: Self-supervised learning of when and how to call APIs (calculator, search, calendar). No human annotation — the model decides when tools help. Defined tool-use as a learned capability.

entries.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
entries.description: Toolformer demonstrated that a language model can learn to use external APIs (calculator, calendar, Wikipedia search, translation) by generating its own training data: sample potential API calls from its own completions, execute them, keep insertions that reduce perplexity, and fine-tune on the result. No human annotations required.

entries.title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
entries.description: GPT-3 was significantly undertrained. Optimal: 20 tokens per parameter. Chinchilla (70B, 1.4T tokens) outperforms Gopher (280B, 300B tokens). Every LLM training decision made after uses these laws.

entries.title: Training Language Models to Follow Instructions with Human Feedback (InstructGPT)
entries.description: RLHF alignment — the technique that made GPT-3 into ChatGPT. SFT + reward model + PPO. Smaller aligned models outperform larger unaligned ones on user preference.

entries.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
entries.description: Extended CoT to tree-structured exploration with backtracking. BFS/DFS over reasoning steps. Solved game of 24 where CoT + self-consistency failed. Defined deliberate reasoning paradigm.

entries.title: Triton: An Intermediate Language and Compiler for Tiled Neural Network Computations
entries.description: Triton lets you write GPU kernels in Python-like syntax at the block level, without C++/CUDA. Custom attention variants, fused activations, and sparse operations that would require weeks in CUDA can be written in hours. FlashAttention-2 and many production kernels are implemented in Triton.

entries.title: U-Net: Convolutional Networks for Biomedical Image Segmentation
entries.description: Defined the encoder-decoder with skip connections architecture. Trained on very small datasets using data augmentation. Dominant in medical imaging for 10 years.

entries.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition (VGGNet)
entries.description: Demonstrated that network depth using only 3×3 convolutions is a critical component for accuracy. Simplicity + depth = the architectural principle that influenced a decade of CNN design.

entries.title: Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition
entries.description: VGGNet â€” proved that depth with uniform 3Ã—3 convolutions is the key to visual representations.

entries.title: Video-LLaMA: An Instruction-Tuned Audio-Visual Language Model for Video Understanding
entries.description: Extends LLaVA's visual instruction tuning to video and audio. Adds a Video Q-Former (sampling frames from video) and an Audio Q-Former (encoding audio from IMAGEBIND) into the Llama language model. Enables video QA, audio QA, and audio-visual QA with a single model. First open-source audio-visual LLM.

entries.title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words
entries.description: ViT — a pure Transformer on image patches matches the best CNNs given sufficient pre-training data.

entries.title: Visual Instruction Tuning (LLaVA)
entries.description: GPT-4 generates visual instruction data → train LLaMA with simple linear projection from CLIP. First fully open-source visual instruction tuning. LLaVA-1.5 matches GPT-4V on several benchmarks.

entries.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
entries.description: LLM agent in Minecraft that continuously explores, learns, and acquires skills without human intervention. Skill library grows without forgetting. Demonstrated curriculum learning via LLM.

entries.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
entries.description: Voyager is an agent that plays Minecraft autonomously. It maintains a skill library — a code base of executable skills (e.g., "mine_diamond", "build_shelter") — and continually writes new skills as LLM-generated JavaScript programs, testing them in the environment. entries.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
entries.description: Standard data parallelism replicates optimizer states and gradients across every GPU — prohibitively expensive for large models. ZeRO partitions these across ranks: Stage 1 partitions optimizer states, Stage 2 adds gradients, Stage 3 adds parameters. ZeRO-3 enables trillion-parameter training on commodity GPU clusters and is the foundation of DeepSpeed.
